question.text: Sundaram Industries Ltd (listed manufacturer) reports the following net profits (computed under Section 198 of Companies Act 2013): FY 2021-22 — INR 40 cr; FY 2022-23 — INR 50 cr; FY 2023-24 — INR 60 cr. For FY 2024-25 CSR budgeting under Section 135, what is the mandatory CSR spend?

answer.text: INR 1.00 crore — 2% of FY 2023-24 net profit only
INR 1.20 crore — 2% of FY 2024-25 projected net profit
INR 1.00 crore — 2% of the 3-year average net profit of INR 50 crore
INR 1.50 crore — 3% of the 3-year average net profit

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 obliges every eligible company to spend at least 2% of the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years on CSR. For Sundaram Industries the three relevant years are FY 2021-22, FY 2022-23, and FY 2023-24, with profits of INR 40, 50, and 60 crore. Average = (40 + 50 + 60) / 3 = INR 50 crore. 2% × INR 50 crore = INR 1 crore. This is the FY 2024-25 mandatory CSR spend. The Trap: Using only FY 2023-24's profit ignores the three-year averaging rule. Using "projected" FY 2024-25 net profit is wrong because the statute uses prior-year actuals. 3% on the average is fabricated; the statutory rate is 2%. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook describes CSR impact-assessment thresholds in general terms but does not, on the cited pages, set out the Section 135 rule that the obligation equals 2% of the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years. That formula is drawn from Section 135(5) of the Companies Act 2013 rather than from the workbook pages checked.
